model: Series AVLV low air velocity transmitter, BACnet MS/TP
applies_to: Dwyer Series AVLV low air velocity transmitters (100-400 FPM ranges) with the BACnet MS/TP option.
summary: The AVLV measures low air velocity and air temperature and can report volumetric flow from a programmed flow area. On BACnet MS/TP it gives velocity and temperature as Analog Inputs in imperial and metric units, flow and flow area as Analog Values, and three Binary Values to start zero, span and factory-reset routines. The MS/TP address is set with a DIP switch.
notes: Flow and flow area are given twice, in imperial and metric units, as separate objects.
The property tables mark AV 4 Flow Area SqM Present_Value as Read/Write but AV 3 Flow Area SqFt as Read; kept as printed.
BV 3 is printed as "Restore Factory Pressure Values"; the text says it restores zero, span and area.
Zero, span and reset each take up to 10 s; the BV stays active on success and drops to inactive on failure.

source.title: Series AVLV Low Air Velocity Transmitter with BACnet Communication - Specifications, Installation and Operating Instructions

integration.summary: Set the MS/TP address on DIP switch SW2, power up so auto-baud can detect the bus, then read velocity (AI 1/2), temperature (AI 3/4) and flow (AV 1/2).
setup: MS/TP address is set on DIP switch SW2 (binary, valid 0-127); factory address is 127.
Auto-baud runs after power-up and after an address change; it completes on the first Who-Is or ReadProperty it answers.
Device instance defaults to 607xxx (xxx = address) until a specific instance is written.
DeviceCommunicationControl and ReinitializeDevice need the password "Dwyer"; Max Master and Max Info Frames changes need a power cycle.
gotchas: Zero (BV 1) only works with no airflow and within ±2% of span of the previous zero.
Span (BV 2) must follow a zero within 5 minutes or it fails.
Flow readings are only right once the flow area matches the duct.
